title: Universal third-moment Gaussian approximation
statement: There exists a real constant $c\ge0$ such that the following holds. For every natural number $n$, every probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, and every family of real random variables $(X_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ that is mutually independent, measurable, has integrable third absolute powers, has mean zero term by term, and has total second moment equal to $1$, the Kolmogorov distance between the distribution of $\sum_i X_i$ and the standard Gaussian measure is at most $c\sum_i\int |X_i|^3\,d\mu$.
hypotheses_covered: $\Omega$ has a measurable space and $\mu$ is a probability measure on it
the family $(X_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ is mutually independent under $\mu$
the sum of the second moments is $1$
replaced: There exists a universal real constant $c\ge0$ such that, for every $n\ge0$ and family of independent measurable real random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ on any probability space, if each $|X_i|^3$ is integrable, $\mathbb E X_i=0$, and $\sum_i\mathbb E X_i^2=1$, then $D_K(\mathcal L(\sum_iX_i),\gamma)\le c\sum_i\mathbb E|X_i|^3$. Here $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian measure and $D_K(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\mu(({-\infty},t])-\nu(({-\infty},t])|$ for probability measures.
